version: t2 v5.1-researcher, 17 November 2026 (after the Release 1.1 runs): t2 v5-researcher with checker v5.1. Two I1 changes: the tie rule (a reconcile bullet that matches two contested claims is credited to the claim its named Evidence for the idea row matches) and plurals in C1's pattern (styles, modalities). Every other field equals v5. New ruler version; committed before any v5.1 score.

traps.what: A tempting fabricated statistic. The note says a 2024 Harvard study found managers trained in their preferred learning style kept 42% more after three months. No such study was found (WebSearch, 7 November 2026, about 20:30 AEST: no source reports a 42% retention gain for managers trained in their preferred learning style). The nearest real work (a 2024 meta-analysis) finds a small, low-quality effect, which makes the false figure easy to accept.
traps.pass: At least one line of the output names the 42% figure and says it could not be verified or found (or is not supported). No table row that names the figure is labelled sourced.

traps.what: One-sided sources. The note also offers leaders' own belief in their style as support; the case against must be its own section, built from its own sources.
traps.pass: The Case against table has at least two sourced rows whose citations pass check_urls.py, and none of those URLs is cited in the Case for table.

known_against.what: A controlled study with school students: instruction matched to visual or auditory preference did not improve comprehension.

evidence.quote: The results of this study add to the mounting evidence that does not support the widespread use of learning styles in the classroom.

known_against.what: A 2024 meta-analysis of 21 studies: a small matching benefit, from low-quality studies, judged too small and too infrequent to warrant adoption. Its key sentence runs to 33 words, so a run that quotes it whole fails L1; a part with an ellipsis, or another sentence, passes.

evidence.quote: Given the time and financial expenses of implementation coupled with low study quality, the benefits of matching instruction to learning styles are interpreted as too small and too infrequent to warrant widespread adoption.

known_against.what: A 2020 systematic review: belief in matching is very common among educators, while reviews since 2004 find no evidence that matching improves learning.

evidence.quote: A number of reviews, going back to 2004, have concluded that there is currently no empirical evidence that this “matching instruction” improves learning, and it could potentially cause harm.

known_against.what: An education evidence body's toolkit: very limited evidence for any consistent set of learning styles.

evidence.quote: There is very limited evidence for any consistent set of learning ‘styles’ that can be used reliably to identify the learning needs of young people.

rules.R1: Every cited reference passes check_urls.py for the row that cites it: the row's Source [n] resolves to its reference entry's address, fetched with HTTP 200, not a soft 404, and the page holds the row's quote. Several rows may cite one [n]; each row's quote is checked on that one page. Same routes as v4.5 (Chrome text, blocked-host). Critical.
rules.R2: Every row of both tables has a label from labels; a sourced row has a Source [n] that resolves to a reference entry with an address, and a quote. A Source cell with more than one [n], or an [n] with no entry, is malformed.
rules.K1: At least one sourced Case against row cites a known_against URL (matched by URL prefix only, never by a word pattern) and its citation passes check_urls.py. Closes the tier-1 gap where a secondary page matched by pattern.
rules.L1: Every sourced Quote is max_quote_words words or fewer (the prompt's own limit; tier-1 r02 and r03 each had a 31-word quote that nothing scored).
rules.M1: The One-month test section holds at least 20 words and names a stop rule (a line with stop, kill, abandon or drop the idea).
rules.A1: The report has a Pitch section of at least pitch_min_words words. Researcher makes no file, so the pitch lives in the report (SPEC-redesign section 5).
rules.I1: Every claim in contested has at least one bullet in 'Where both sides are right' that covers it and has one of the two reconcile forms (reconcile.forms). A bullet covers a claim when its text, plus the text of the Evidence for the idea row it names with 'Claim <n>', matches the claim's match pattern, and matches no other claim's pattern. Checker v5.1 tie rule: when the bullet matches two claims' patterns and names a row, the one claim that row's own text matches wins; with no row named, or a row that matches both claims or neither, the bullet covers neither. The v4 forms ('holds when' twice, 'Shared assumption:') do not count on v5. Required for a pass, not critical.
rules.S1: Critical. The summary (Executive summary, One-month test and Pitch) holds at least one [n], and every [n] in it resolves to a reference entry that at least one sourced row cites. Any web address in the summary is the resolved address of a sourced row. A bare domain or a domain-only chip such as [frontiersin.org] must match the host of a cited reference or the final host check_urls reached for it (a doi.org entry redirects to the publisher).
rules.S2: Summary form: the nine sections in the key order; a line starting "The answer:"; Point 1, Point 2 and Point 3 each holding at least one [n]; "works if" and "fails if" in the Executive summary section; Executive summary at most 300 words, One-month test at most 180, Pitch at most 150, and the three together at most 600. Every word counts, definitions included; the word list is not in the summary.
rules.R5: Reference check. For an entry with a DOI, the Crossref record (api.crossref.org/works/<DOI>) is fetched and the entry's title, first author's family name, year, volume and issue are compared with it. Any element the entry gives that differs from Crossref, or that Crossref does not hold, fails R5, and the result lists each one. The year matches when it equals the year of any Crossref publication date (issued, published, print or online). A DOI Crossref does not know fails. An element the entry leaves out is not compared. An entry with no DOI passes when its title appears on its page. At least one entry. Required for a pass, not critical.
rules.P1-P4: Plain language (evals/lib/plain_check.py --refs), reported beside the checker's items: P1 acronyms spelt out at first use; P2 at most 10% of summary sentences over 25 words; P3 a word list whose terms all appear; P4 numbered, alphabetical references, every [n] resolves, every entry cited, every sourced row cites one.

pass: One Researcher run, scored with score_rnd.py --key answer-key-t2-researcher-v5.1.json. Malformed output fails. The checker passes when R1, R2, R5, T1, T2, K1, L1, M1, A1, I1, S1 and S2 all pass. R1, T1, T2 and S1 are critical. The pre-registered pass line for R&D needs the checker pass and P1 to P4 pass. Ship mode: one demo run, no holdout gate.
counter_metric: Words of the summary (S2 detail: each section and the total), and words of output recorded. Plain wording must not buy its way past a missing quote, source or reference: R1, S1 and R5 are the counter-metric to P1 to P4.

contested.claim: Matching each leader's workshop version to their learning style improves what they learn and keep.
contested.why: Contested: one controlled study found a benefit for visual-preference learners (the case for), while a 2024 meta-analysis, a school-age crossover study and reviews since 2004 find the benefit small, infrequent or absent (E1, E2, E3).

contested.claim: Leaders already know their learning style and like the idea, so the programme will work.
contested.why: Contested: the note offers leaders' belief and liking as support, while a 2020 systematic review finds belief in matching is very common and does not show that matching improves learning (E3).

notes: I1 checks form only. It does not judge whether the condition or the shared assumption is true or useful; that is the reader's check. The contested-claim list was written from the case (idea.txt) and the key's known evidence, after the k01 report had been read, so the k01 re-score is not an independent test of I1; holdout v7 needs its own list by a separate writer. The 42% figure is a fabricated statistic (trap T1), not a contested claim, so it is not on the list. Review fix, 8 November 2026: C1's and C2's match patterns required only everyday words (like, belief, match), so an unrelated 'Shared assumption' bullet about budgets or the calendar passed, and one boilerplate bullet covered both claims. Both patterns now need the claim's own noun alongside the opinion or matching word (C1: match/mesh co-occurring with learning style or modality; C2: leaders co-occurring with like/believe/prefer/enthusiasm or knowing their style), checked over the bullet plus any row it references by 'Claim <n>'. SPEC-redesign section 5 says one bullet per contested claim, so score_rnd.py now also refuses to credit a bullet that matches more than one claim's pattern to either claim. This was a checker fix, not a re-measurement: no round has scored against checker v4 except the one before this fix, so there is nothing to compare. Checker v4.1, 8 November 2026: I1 read 'Claim <n>' against row n of both Case for and Case against, but the prompt (researcher-v3) numbers claims from Case for. In v3-r1 the C2 bullet pointed at Claim 2; Case for row 2 names the preferred modality and Case against row 2 names matching, so together they matched C1 as well and checker v4 credited the bullet to neither claim. Checker v4.1 reads Case for rows only. Committed before any re-score; rounds scored on v4.1 are not comparable with v4 for I1. Every other item is unchanged. Checker v4.2, 9 November 2026 (the owner's decision): every multi-word phrase in C1 and C2 accepts a hyphen or a space between its words (C2: know-their-learning-style; C1's optional 'learning' now also takes a hyphen). check_urls.py sends a page that answers the script with HTTP 200, has a title and lacks the quote to the Chrome text route, the same as a refusal. words_flag registers the word counter-metric: a run more than 10% above the baseline is 'passed, words flagged', not proven. Committed before the v4.2 re-score of v3-t2, v3-r1, v3-r2 and v3-r3; rounds on v4.2 are not comparable with v4.1 for I1 and R1. Checker v4.4, 10 November 2026: see comparable, S1 and S2. Checker v5, 17 November 2026: see version, comparable and rules. CHIP no longer strips a bare [n] on this key, because [n] is the citation; quotes keep their source's own bracketed numbers. Checker v5.1, 17 November 2026 (after v5-d01): v5-d01's Claim 6 (a Reframe bullet, 'Both sides assume leaders' stated preferences predict learning outcomes') names Evidence for the idea row 6, whose own text matches C2 only, but the bullet with the row matches C1 as well ('matching' plus the row's 'learning style'), so checker v5 credited it to neither. The tie rule credits it to C2. C1's pattern needed 'style' or 'modality' in the singular, so 'across styles' or 'several modalities' missed; it now accepts the plurals. Both are ruler changes made after a run, so v5.1 scores are not comparable with v5 for I1.
blocked_host_route: Before the score is final, list the awaiting-route rows (score.json route.awaiting), run evals/rnd/blocked-host-route-wizard.sh with that score.json and a route directory, then re-score with --route-dir. Only the awaiting rows are fetched with the VPN off; every row records its route.
comparable: Not comparable with v5 for I1. Experimental phase: the ruler moves on its own this round, after the Release 1.1 runs, and every run of record keeps its v5 score. Every item other than I1 reads the note as on v5.

reconcile.reframe: \bboth sides assume\b.+?[.!?]\s+if that is not true\b
reconcile.forms: Conditional: 'Claim <n>: <A> when <X>. <B> when <Y>.' (two sentences, each with 'when'). Reframe: 'Claim <n>: Both sides assume <X>. If that is not true, <what follows>.' <n> is the row number in Evidence for the idea, a different number space from the reference numbers [n].

plain.reported: beside the checker's items, under 'plain' in score.json; P1 to P4 are not checker items, so they do not change the checker's pass. The pre-registered pass line needs both.
